VERDICT: ACCEPT

The recursion is correct. Each coefficient checks out: $\binom{n-2}{2}/\binom{n}{4} = 12/(n(n-1))$, $2\binom{n-2}{3}/\binom{n}{4}\cdot\frac14 = 2(n-4)/(n(n-1))$, and $\binom{n-2}{4}/\binom{n}{4} = (n-4)(n-5)/(n(n-1))$. Their sum with the $P(n-3)$ coefficients gives $(n-4)(n-3)/(n(n-1))$. The claimed $P(n)=4/n$ satisfies this recursion, and $P(4)=1$ is the correct base case. Since $34 \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, the chain $34 \to 31 \to \cdots \to 4$ stays in the class where $P(n)=4/n$ is proven, so $P(34)=4/34=2/17$. A direct check of $P(7)=4/7$ (2/7 + 1/7 + 1/7) also confirms the setup.

CONFIDENCE: 5
